Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  April 4, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on April 4, 2023. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present  Commissioner Lee Denmon – District 1, Cynthia McLemore – District
  3, Commissioner Christopher Beck – District 4, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large
  Absent  Commissioner Octavio Padilla – District 2

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director
  Gilbert Gonzalez  Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Geoffrey Okamoto  Human Services Program Manager – Transit
  Operations
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Teresa Estrada  Recreation Superintendent

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner
McLemore that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on June
1, 2023, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Brown that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on August 3, 2023, be
approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Brown that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on October 5, 2023, be
approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, McLemore, Beck, and Denmon
Noes: None

   Park and Recreation Commission

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Graffiti Abatement Supervisor, Gilbert Gonzalez
reported the following: During the month of April, his crew power washed the ground
around the baseball bleachers and repainted the bleachers for Inglewood Little Leagues
Opening day at Rogers Park. In District 2, the alleys were vandalize back to back just west
of Prairie from Century to Kelso. District 4 was also vandalized near Yukon and Doty from
Imperial to Century. Staff replaced a missing section of a bridge on the play equipment at
Ashwood Park. A new pump for the splash pad was installed at Ashwood Park and a broken
slide was replaced at a playground at Vincent Park. The graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. The Human Services Program Manager – Transit
Operations, Geoffrey Okamoto reported the following: Nutrition: We are serving
approximately 450 seniors per week through home-delivered meals for homebound
seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. We continue to provide fresh
produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute. We served a
special Easter Brunch this month, which included glazed ham, and a delightful pineapple
upside-down cake. We will be serving a special meal on May 5 for Cinco de Mayo, which
will include Steak Picado, Pinto Beans, Green Salad with sliced Tomatoes, Spanish Brown
Rice, Tortilla, and Mandarin Oranges with Jicama. Senior Center Operations: Our Black and
White Gala on March 15, 2024, had over 200 seniors in attendance. Our seniors were
treated as royals by our incredible staff. Our seniors have praised how much they enjoyed
themselves, the food, the music, and how elegant the Magnolia room looked. The Mayor,
Councilwoman Faulk, Councilwoman Grey and Councilman Padilla attended. On March 21,
2024, the Tree people a non-profit organization gave a presentation on how to care for
fruit trees and afterwards distributed 80 fruit trees to our seniors. On March 29, 2024, 40
seniors received booster shots from the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health.
On April 4, 2024, 36 seniors and four (4) chaperones attended the Giuseppe Verdi’s La
Traviata. Seniors were first transported to Ashwood Park were they enjoyed their packed
lunch before heading to the LA Opera. On April, 5, 2024, the legal nonprofit Bet Tzedek will
be conducting an Advance Planning presentation to seniors interested in estate planning.
Upcoming events include: May 3rd the celebration of Cinco de Mayo with a special meal
(Steak Picado) and May 10th the celebration of Mother’s Day. Senior Transportation: Our
paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors and the disabled community in
and around Inglewood and Hawthorne. The Metro Micro on-demand service recently
increased their fare (3/24/24) from $1.00 to $2.50, however for seniors and the disabled;
the fare will continue to be $1.00. This provides service to the area of LAX/Inglewood
among other locations around the county. Finally, we are in the process of promoting two
(2) of our part time drivers to full time bus operator status. We have also been providing
refresher training on wheelchair lift operation and securement procedures to ensure that
bus operators are well informed, not only on how to operate the lifts effectively but to also

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

ensure they are securing the wheelchairs effectively as well. CACFP: The Child and Adult
Care Food Program (CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at
Crenshaw Library, Inglewood Main Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park. The program's
hours are Monday through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks
from 4:30 PM - 5:00 PM. We serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week.

REPORTS - RECREATION. Recreation Superintendent, Teresa Estrada reported the
following: INGLEWOOD STEM FEST: The department is excited to host the 3rd Annual
Inglewood STEM Fest in partnership with Science of Sport. The event will be held on
Saturday, April 20 from 9:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the Edward Vincent Park (Champions
Field). This free event will expose students in grades Kindergarten through sixth to science,
technology, engineering, and math (STEM) through unique experiences that focus on
several familiar sports. This event is designed to bring in Los Angeles-based sports
organizations to provide an engaging day of STEM and sports to the Inglewood community.
Activity stations will be set up throughout the event providing STEM lessons centered
around basketball, soccer, tennis, baseball, softball, football, golf, volleyball, and track &
field. This event continues to grow and get better each year. In 2022 we served 250 kids,
2023 had 500 participants and this year we are preparing for up to 700 kids. Community
partners for the event include the Los Angeles Chargers, Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation,
Angel City Football Club, Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Rams, and Los Angeles Clippers
to name a few. Be sure to mark your calendars for this awesome event! BEGINNING
PHOTOGRAPHY: The Spring session the beginning photography classes will begin on April
23rd. Students will learn the basics of camera operation and fundamental concepts of
photography. Classes will focus on developing visual literacy skills and non-verbal forms
of creative expression. Students will be introduced to basic photographic components as
they learn how to use cameras and experiment with telling a story through images. Classes
are held on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 4:00 – 5:30 p.m. at the Veterans Memorial
Building. The cost is $80 per student. Interested participants can register online at
parksrec.cityofinglewood.org. For more information on our Inglewood Youth Sports
Leagues, visit our city sports website at: https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. Thomas Uwal, Director reported on the following Capital
Improvement updates: Stormwater Improvement Project: There was an outreach
meeting for the Stormwater Improvement Project at Edward Vincent Park. There are also
a couple of outreach meetings scheduled for the month of April and May so the community
can give their input and feedback. Both Councilman Padilla and Councilwoman Gray are
invited to attend the meetings. Staff continues to discuss the amenities that the public
suggested. This is an ongoing project. Vincent Park Soccer Field Parking Lot Improvement
Project: The City Council awarded the project to Voltaire Engineering on March 26, 2024
for $191,050. The project is expected to be completed in September 2024. Darby Park
Walking Track: The Darby Park Walking track project was completed this year. The

   Park and Recreation Commission

community is excited and we can see residents enjoying and walking on the new track. We
are looking forward to holding a formal opening ceremony for the community very soon.
Rogers Park Fencing: There was a fencing panel broken at Rogers Park. Our Park
maintenance crew replaced the fence as soon as they were made aware about the broken
fence. The users of the Park are very appreciative to our maintenance crew for addressing
the issue quickly.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. Jose Palomares thanks staff for the bike racks and picnic tables
throughout Vincent Park. He was also thankful for the lights being fixed and looks forward
to the renovation of the parking lot at Vincent Park. Lastly, Mr. Palomares suggested
installation of cameras outside of the restrooms.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Denmon proposed bike racks placed at all
the parks. Commissioner Beck suggested locking the parking lot gates at Darby Park; he
also mentioned how he noticed that other parks are lit up with lighting and recommended
more lights around the restroom areas. Finally, Commissioner Beck suggested additional
patrolling as a deterrent. Mr. Palomares suggested adding Park Rangers.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:53 p.m.
